data.narrative:
Sereact, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ralf Gulde and Marc Tuscher, has raised $140M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public (277810.KQ) and eight private—including same-stage peers Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $140M total raised as a proxy base, implying a valuation of $266M. The peer-median approach references three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B. The median of this peer set is $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B.

The two methods diverge significantly, producing a triangulated range of $226M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The stage-progression approach yields a substantially lower estimate than peer comparables, reflecting the tension between capital-to-date and market valuations for similarly-staged peers. Key uncertainties include revenue scale and growth trajectory relative to the peer set, which would materially influence positioning within this range. The wide dispersion underscores the need for revenue or unit economics data to tighten the valuation band.
